tierWhy: measurement and reconciliation of two instruments; no money path, no ship-gate review
subject: Does A's five-cut fix halve the leak on b103, and are the PO's numbers comparable to mine
headline: The halving does not survive either instrument. By the PO's own series the rate is flat across builds; by mine the five cuts move it 12.5%.

theHalvingClaim.asStated: PO 12 MB/cycle on b103 versus C's pre-fix 23.5 MB/cycle, read as a 2x reduction
theHalvingClaim.problem: that compares two different instruments on two different builds with two different workloads

poOwnSeriesAcrossBuilds.reading: flat; about -5% from b99 to b103, no step change

theHalvingClaim.conclusion: both instruments independently say the five cuts did not halve anything. The 12-vs-23.5 gap is an instrument gap that predates the fix: the PO read 13.3 on b85 while I read 23.5 on the same class of build.

q1_whichCutCarried.answer: cut 2, host orderManager registries. The other four carry nothing on this build.
q1_whichCutCarried.reading: disabling cut 2 returns the rate to the control; disabling cut 1 does not degrade at all
q1_whichCutCarried.cuts345: no hook to call at collapse: _timeframeFetchAbort falsy, no live _indicatorWorkerSingleton, TalariaCustomIndicators.disposeWorker absent on all four panels (live RELEASE-TARGET-CENSUS, not a grep)
q1_whichCutCarried.deadWeightIntoCanary: cuts 1, 3, 4, 5 — keep the kill-switches, but nothing measurable is lost by their absence
q1_whichCutCarried.honestLimit: n=1 per arm; within-run spread reaches 4.5 MB against a 3.06 MB effect, so three repeats per arm would settle it

q2_isPanelBStillSurviving.answer: YES, in every configuration measured on b103
q2_isPanelBStillSurviving.perDirectorsOwnRule: B still survives, so the cuts were incomplete rather than the remaining mass being a wholly separate mechanism

remainingMassNamed.class: a HOST cache holding an object that was ALLOCATED INSIDE a panel realm; the object's constructor and prototype belong to that realm, so one cached item pins the whole ~20.87MB realm
remainingMassNamed.instance2_local: the host bar cache: closure put -> context files Map -> tfs Map -> bars Array -> a bar object -> constructor -> the panel realm global
remainingMassNamed.whyCapsNeverWorked: a cap bounds how many items the cache holds, not which realm a single held item reaches. This is why the ten cache shots in W74 did not move the rate.
remainingMassNamed.cutShape: copy bars and ref-owner entries into host-realm objects on ingest, or key those caches by realm and evict on removeChart

q3_does15PairsChangeTheComparison.answer: The numbers are NOT directly comparable as per-cycle means. They are comparable as totals over a stated cycle count, and they are comparable in mechanism.

reasons.reason: my rate decays with cycle count, so any per-cycle mean depends on how long you ran
reasons.consequence: a 3-cycle run reads about 21-22 and a 5-cycle tail reads 19.4. A longer or heavier session sits lower on that curve, which moves the PO's session toward a smaller per-cycle number without any change in mechanism.

reasons.evidence: every floor I quote is taken after HeapProfiler.collectGarbage; the PO reads the live number. His deltas are +16, +3, +27, +6, +9 — the jitter signature of GC landing between readings, where mine are smooth.
reasons.consequence: his robust statistic is the total (+61 over five cycles), not any single delta; per-cycle means from a live reading and from a forced-GC floor are different quantities.

reasons.reason: panel count should NOT scale the leak, so 15 pairs is not the explanation
reasons.evidence: retention is exactly ONE realm per cycle and it is slot-bound to panel B — dataset rotation moved the data and B still survived. Growth is quantised in ~20.87MB realm units.
reasons.consequence: his +61 MB over five cycles is about three realms; my +95 MB over four cycles is about four and a half. Same quantum, different frequency; a 15-pair session does not retain 15 realms per cycle.

q3_does15PairsChangeTheComparison.howToCompareProperly: state the build, the cycle count, and whether GC was forced, then compare TOTAL growth. On b103: PO +61MB / 5 cycles live-read, C +95MB / 4 cycles forced-GC floor.
q3_does15PairsChangeTheComparison.harnessLimit: my harness expands to four panels only (expandFourPanelsWithRetry / waitForDistV9FourReady), so I cannot reproduce a 15-pair session to test it directly. Saying so rather than implying the shapes match.

snapshotCeiling.note: the five-cycle run is floor-only, no heap snapshots taken, so the V8 max-string-length ceiling does not apply to it. Snapshot-bearing runs remain at 3 cycles; 6 dies.
